title: Restoration of the Y220C p53 Full-Length Mutant by PK11000: a Molecular Dynamics Study of an Intrinsically Disordered Protein.
authors: Stetson, Sean; Caballero Mancia, Fernando; Thayer, Kelly M
one_liner_zh: 该研究用分子动力学模拟全长p53（含无序N/C端区域），揭示Y220C突变与PK11000小分子通过长程变构影响DBD稳定性及无序区域介导的调控机制，直接契合无序蛋白互作机制建模主题。
abstract: The tumor suppressor protein p53 plays a key role in cellular homeostasis, with its dysfunction linked to over half of all cases of human cancer. The Y220C mutation in the DNA-binding domain (DBD) destabilizes p53, compromising its function. The most well-studied case of Y220C p53 rescue via a small molecule, PK11000, has been shown to restore stability and reinstate activity both in vitro and in vivo in rodent models. While prior in silico studies have focused on the DBD in isolation, this work explores the full-length p53 protein, incorporating its intrinsically disordered N- and C-terminal regulatory regions, which are known to be sites of extensive post-translational modifications utilized to modulate its activity. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we investigate the wild-type (WT) p53, the destabilized Y220C mutant, and the PK11000-rescued Y220C variant. Our findings illuminate a multilayered allosteric landscape: the Y220C mutation disrupts DBD stability through long-range effects while PK11000 counteracts this destabilization through its own distal interactions. Importantly, the N- and C-terminal regions mediate additional allosteric regulation, dynamically influencing both the mutation's impact and the rescue mechanism. This triple allosteric framework underscores the regulatory regions' critical role in restoring p53 functionality. By providing a first-order exploration into the behavior of full-length p53, this study advances our understanding of its regulatory mechanisms and sets the stage for developing targeted therapies aimed at reactivating mutant p53 in cancer.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤抑制蛋白p53在细胞稳态中发挥关键作用，其功能失调与超过半数的人类癌症病例相关。DNA结合域（DBD）中的Y220C突变使p53不稳定，损害其功能。通过小分子PK11000拯救Y220C p53的最深入研究案例已显示，在体外及啮齿动物模型体内均能恢复稳定性并重新激活其活性。尽管先前的计算机模拟研究聚焦于孤立的DBD，本研究则探索全长p53蛋白，纳入其 intrinsically disordered 的N端和C端调控区域，这些区域已知是广泛翻译后修饰的位点，用于调节其活性。利用分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，我们研究了野生型 (WT) p53、不稳定的Y220C突变体以及PK11000拯救的Y220C变体。我们的发现揭示了一个多层次变构景观：Y220C突变通过长程效应破坏DBD稳定性，而PK11000则通过其自身的远端相互作用抵消这种去稳定化。重要的是，N端和C端区域介导额外的变构调控，动态影响突变的影响和拯救机制。这一三重变构框架强调了调控区域在恢复p53功能中的关键作用。通过对全长p53行为的初步探索，本研究增进了对其调控机制的理解，并为开发旨在重新激活癌症中突变p53的靶向治疗奠定了基础。
